novel_features.name: All-logs fan-out for a request
novel_features.description: One command fetches the per-request devLog, the runtime Log.txt, and the engine build log, in order.
novel_features.rationale: The three logs live on two different presigned-S3 hops that 302 away from the API host; nothing today fetches them together.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When a predict fails you want every log granularity at once, not three manual URL dances that break if you send the auth header to S3.

novel_features.name: One-command long-description upload
novel_features.description: Publish a model's long description from a Markdown file in one step, including the S3 upload dance.
novel_features.rationale: The console hides a presign -> PUT -> upsert chain behind its rich-text editor; no CLI or SDK exposes it.
novel_features.example: unitypredict-pp-cli models describe set c6985b70-15e0-4ba9-8cb1-128200595a8f --file README.md
novel_features.why_it_matters: The long description is a hosted file, not a text field — writing prose into the upsert body is silently ignored, so automation needs the exact 3-step chain.

novel_features.name: Declarative inputs/outcomes
novel_features.description: Define a model's input and outcome variables from a YAML file instead of the console's per-field editors.
novel_features.rationale: aiEngineConfig plus variableDisplayOptions is the most error-prone payload on the platform; a partial upsert silently clobbers it.
novel_features.example: unitypredict-pp-cli models io set c6985b70-15e0-4ba9-8cb1-128200595a8f --from io.yaml
novel_features.why_it_matters: The GET-mutate-POST full-record discipline and the hidden-variable display map are only automatable if one command owns the whole round-trip.

novel_features.name: Reverse lookup: models per engine
novel_features.description: List every model built on a given engine.
novel_features.rationale: The engineId= query param on list routes is silently ignored, so this is unanswerable without the dedicated route.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Before redeploying or deleting an engine you must know its blast radius; the console buries this.

novel_features.name: Honest auth check
novel_features.description: Validate credentials against the one endpoint that cannot lie about auth.
novel_features.rationale: List endpoints return 200 for a garbage bearer; only GET /api/engines/{bare-uuid} separates bad key (401) from unknown id (404).
novel_features.why_it_matters: Prevents shipping on a wrong-env or malformed key that appeared to work because a list route answered 200.

novel_features.name: Engine concurrency view
novel_features.description: Show how many engine nodes ran in parallel over time, as a table.
novel_features.rationale: The stats live inside stateInfo.historicalNodeCountStats on the engine record; only the console Stats page renders them today.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Answers capacity questions (did we actually run 4 in parallel?) without the console.

novel_features.name: Invoke, wait, download in one call
novel_features.description: Invoke a model with text or file inputs, poll to completion, and pull File outcomes into a directory.
novel_features.rationale: The invoke->poll->presigned-download chain spans 6 routes and two no-auth S3 hops; the SDK needs a script to do it.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Cold-started GPU models take minutes; a single wait-and-fetch command is the difference between a script and a one-liner.

novel_features.name: Cross-environment diff
novel_features.description: Compare a model or engine record across dev and prod, field by field.
novel_features.rationale: Two Auth0 tenants with separate keys; no existing tool can query both in one step.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Before promoting, you want to know exactly which fields drifted between dev and prod.

narrative.headline: The console-only parts of UnityPredict — model authoring, long descriptions, IO config, cross-env diffing — as CLI commands.
narrative.value_prop: UnityPredict's engine lifecycle has a Python SDK, but creating models, editing metadata, uploading long descriptions, and configuring inputs/outcomes are console-only. This CLI wraps the full sniffed API surface, including the presigned-S3 flows that break when auth rides along, and adds a dev/prod-aware safety guard.
narrative.auth_narrative: Durable API keys live in ~/.unitypredict/credentials keyed dev/prod; the header needs the literal APIKEY@ prefix (plain keys 401 on strict routes). --env dev|prod selects the tenant; prod mutations refuse without --i-know.

quickstart.comment: Prove the key works against the one endpoint that cannot lie
See your models and grab a MODEL id
Reverse lookup: which models use this engine

troubleshoots.symptom: 401 "You cannot use this model without logging in!"
troubleshoots.fix: Auth header missing the literal APIKEY@ prefix — the CLI adds it; check the key in ~/.unitypredict/credentials
You used an ENGINE id; predict needs the MODEL id (console /models/<id>/view)
Presigned URLs must be fetched with no Authorization header — the CLI drops it on cross-host redirects
Wrong-env key returns empty results, not an error; run auth check --env prod

narrative.when_to_use: Deploying, configuring, or invoking UnityPredict models; editing model metadata or IO contracts; diagnosing failed predicts via logs; comparing dev vs prod before promotion.
anti_triggers: Deploying engine images (use the first-party unitypredict SDK CLI)
Account/API-key management (POST /api/auth is excluded — it clobbers the account record on partial bodies)
